messages.subject: Re: FYI on Unicode
messages.body_plain:
Perhaps I'm coming in late on this thread, since I can't discern exactly what problem prompted the discussion, but I've been moderately successful getting unicode symbols to plot in R in Windows (and it works seamlessly for me in Linux).  Here is an excerpt from an old tutorial I wrote about it, geared toward getting IPA glyphs on the plot, but should work for any arbitrary unicode points, provided you have a typeface that actually has glyphs mapped at those codepoints:

# LINUX
par(mfcol=c(1,1), mar=c(1,1,6.5,4.5), family="Charis SIL")
# then run your plotting commands...

# MAC: use the same command as Linux, but beware that for some reason, the Quartz window
# is resistant to having its parameters changed this way, so after running this line, go
# into the menu: R > Preferences > Quartz and change the plotting location from its default
# to whatever you want, and then change it back. I don't know why this works, but it does.

# WINDOWS: fonts can't be directly called through "par()" without first defining a new family.
# The "windowsFonts" command defines a new font family (that I'm calling "ipa") that can then
# be referenced in later lines. Make sure you actually have the Charis SIL font installed or
# this won't work (you can get it here: http://scripts.sil.org/CharisSIL_download).
# Or alternatively, use some other font that has coverage of the IPA glyph range.
windowsFonts(ipa=windowsFont("Charis SIL"))
par(mfcol=c(1,1), mar=c(1,1,6.5,4.5), family="ipa")

The whole tutorial is here:
http://depts.washington.edu/phonlab/resources/plottingVowelsWithConfidenceEllipses.r
...although the ellipse drawing part of it won't work anymore because one of the dependency packages is now defunct.  I slapped together my own package as a placeholder to get me through graduate school, which seems to work well with clean data but has a few limitations and bugs (working on a new version):
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phonR/index.html
http://depts.washington.edu/phonlab/pubs/McCloy2012_phonR.pdf

The most common problem I've heard from windows users is "how to get from Excel into R when there are non-ASCII glyphs in my data".  For that, the solution I've found is:
1.  export from excel as "unicode text".  This will encode as "UCS-2 little endian".
2.  open in Notepad++ or a similarly sophisticated text editor that allows you to change encodings.
3.  Change encoding to "UTF-8 without BOM" and save
4.  open in R using: read.delim("my_utf8_without_bom_file.csv", encoding="UTF-8").
The non-ASCII glyphs will show up in the data frame as bracketed codepoints like this:  <U+025B>
... but if you then specify a font that has those codepoints mapped, you'll get the proper symbols on the plot.

HTH
-- dan

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] goodness-of-fit
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I simply enlarged the margin parameter to margin = c(22, 12) and it worked fine on my maschine (see attachment). Was that your problem or am I missing sth?

Best
Martin

p.s.: here is your updated code:

Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "russian")

# Read file
data <- read.delim( 'http://kjc-fs-cluster.kjc.uni-heidelberg.de/dcs/data/syllables/syllables.dat', sep=";", header=TRUE, comment.char="#", stringsAsFactors=FALSE);
# Groups - ignore the bad data for now
#groups <- data.frame(rbind(
#    c("Gutturals", "k|g|G"),
#    c("Palatals",  "c|j|J"),
#    c("Retroflexes", "T|D|N"),
#    c("Dentals",    "t|d|n"),
#    c("Labials",    "p|b|m")
#), stringsAsFactors=FALSE);

# В правильной последовательности выводятся
groups <- data.frame(rbind(
  c("Лабиальные",    "p|b|m"),
  c("Дентальные",    "t|d|n"),
  c("Церебральные", "T|D|N"),
  c("Палатальные",  "c|j|J"),
  c("Гуттуральные", "k|g|G")
), stringsAsFactors=FALSE);

# Null matrix of pvalues
matpvals <- matrix( numeric(), 0, 5 );
# The total number of syllables for each period
ns <- as.vector( colSums( data[,2:6] ) );
for(i in 1:nrow(groups))
{
    # Filter rows with this group
    g <- grep(groups[i,2], data$Syllable, ignore.case=FALSE);
    sub <- data[g,];
    # The number of syllables containing syllable of this group
    xs <- as.vector( colSums( sub[,2:6] ) );
    # Combined test across all periods
    pval1 <- prop.test( xs, ns )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Early and Epic periods
    pval2 <- prop.test( xs[1:2], ns[1:2] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Epic and Classical periods
    pval3 <- prop.test( xs[2:3], ns[2:3] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across Classical and Medieval periods
    pval4 <- prop.test( xs[3:4], ns[3:4] )$`p.value`;
    # Test across and Late periods
    pval5 <- prop.test( xs[4:5], ns[4:5] )$`p.value`;
    # Combine test results into one vector
    pvalues <- c( pval1, pval2, pval3, pval4, pval5 );
    # Add row for this group to the matrix
    matpvals <- rbind( matpvals, pvalues );
};
# Matrix to data frame
matpvals <- data.frame( matpvals, row.names=groups$X1 );
# Assign row names
# names( matpvals ) <- c( 'All periods', 'Early & Epic', 'Epic & Classical', 'Classical & Medieval', 'Medieval & Late' );

# Русские названия эпох
names( matpvals ) <- c( 'Все эпохы санскрита', 'Веды и эпический', 'Эпический и классический', 'Классический и средневековий', 'Средневековий и поздний' );
# Display matrix
matpvals

# Gasuns plot
data_matrix <- data.matrix(matpvals)
data_heatmap <- heatmap(data_matrix, Rowv=NA, Colv=NA, col = cm.colors(256), scale="column", margins=c(22,12))
# http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=12022
data_heatmap <- heatmap(data_matrix, Rowv=NA, Colv=NA, col = colorRampPalette(c("white","grey","black"))(256), scale="column", margins=c(22,12))
# Different aprroach
# heatmap.2(as.matrix(data_matrix),col =
#            colorRampPalette(c("white","green","green4","violet","purple"))(100))
